title: Knight Dialer
summary: Given an integer n, determine the number of distinct phone numbers of length n that can be dialed using a chess knight's unique movement on a phone pad.
statement: Given an integer n, determine the number of distinct phone numbers of length n that can be dialed using a chess knight's unique movement on a phone pad. The knight can start on any numeric cell and make n-1 valid knight jumps. The result should be returned modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Start on any digit and make n-1 chess-knight moves on a phone keypad.
Return the number of length-n dial strings modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def knight_dialer_count(n):
 moves=((4,6),(6,8),(7,9),(4,8),(0,3,9),(),(0,1,7),(2,6),(1,3),(2,4));dp=[1]*10
 for _ in range(n-1):dp=[sum(dp[x] for x in moves[d])%1000000007 for d in range(10)]
 return sum(dp)%1000000007

hints: Treat keypad digits as graph vertices joined by knight moves.
Track how many sequences of the current length end at each digit.
For each additional digit, sum counts from its knight neighbors.
Every longer sequence has exactly one previous endpoint and one legal final edge.
editorial: Every longer sequence has exactly one previous endpoint and one legal final edge.

tests.explanation: Every digit is a valid one-digit number, giving ten.
There are twenty legal directed knight moves between keypad digits.
